text:
leah (AE): Hey team, AcmeHealth POC needs Private/VPC access for the Redwood private deployment. They're ready to start tomorrow. Need clear list of what to ask from them and what we’ll provision on our side. TL;DR: HIPAA customer, cross-account setup, want minimal network changes.

jules (SE): Quick checklist to collect from them first:
- AWS Account ID(s) for the VPC where endpoints will live
- VPC CIDR(s) and per-AZ subnet CIDR for interface endpoints (we suggest /26 per AZ)
- Which AZs they want us in (must match our allowed AZs)
- Do they prefer VPC Peering or PrivateLink (interface endpoint)? PrivateLink is usually easier for enterprise with restricted route policies.
- Whether they want inbound-only (control-plane in our account) or fully private with data plane in their VPC.
- Any egress restrictions / proxy so we know allowed destination ports/IPs
- TLS inspection or DPI in path? (if yes, may require additional routing)
- KMS key ARN if they want us to use customer-managed CMK for artifacts/logs

Also need: a single contact and cross-account role name we can assume during provisioning.

raj (Network Eng): My take: For AcmeHealth (HIPAA) I'd recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoint) so they don't have to change route tables or allow inbound peering routes. PrivateLink limits blast radius and keeps their VPC routing intact. Caveats:
- ENI quota: interface endpoints create ENIs in subnets. We need them to confirm available ENI quota per AZ.
- IP capacity: each endpoint takes at least one IP per AZ; plan for retries and failover so reserve 5-10 IPs per subnet.
- SGs: we'll require an SG on the endpoint with inbound TCP 443 from our service IP ranges (or use customer SG allowing our service ENIs).

ami (Cloud Ops): Practical provisioning steps (PrivateLink path):
1) We create an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) + endpoint service in our account and share the service name with them (com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxx).
2) Customer creates Interface VPC Endpoint referencing that service in chosen subnets.
3) Customer sends endpoint accept (if configured requireAcceptance) or we auto-accept.
4) They attach SG to endpoint allowing 443 from our service.
5) DNS: we will provide a private hosted zone entry they can bind to route to the vpce, or they can keep split-horizon to map production hostnames to private IPs.

jules (SE): Minimal sample policy & items to send them (copy/paste friendly):
- What we need from AcmeHealth:
  - aws_account_id=123456789012
  - vpc_cidr=10.10.0.0/16
  - subnets=[10.10.1.0/26,10.10.2.0/26] (one per AZ)
  - allowed_ports=443

- IAM trust snippet for cross-account role we ask them to create (if they prefer role vs NAT):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::OUR_ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood-provisioner"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

- Example SG rule (on their endpoint SG):
  - Type: HTTPS, Protocol: TCP, Port: 443, Source: sg-xxxxxxxx (our service SG) or specific CIDR ranges.

- Example CLI to create VPC endpoint (customer side):
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-01234567 --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-abcdefgh --subnet-ids subnet-01234567 subnet-089abcdef --security-group-ids sg-0abc1234
```

leah (AE): Great — they'll likely push back on creating endpoints in prod VPC. They asked if we can do peering instead so they don't touch DNS. What do we say?

raj (Network Eng): Peering pros/cons:
- Pros: Simpler DNS (no private hosted zone mapping), direct routing for all traffic, works with services that don't support PrivateLink.
- Cons: Requires route table edits across subnets, can create asymmetric routing if they have NAT gateways, and cross-account peering requires explicit route entries which many security teams dislike. Peering also exposes more of their VPC to our IPs.

jules (SE): For HIPAA customers I'd still nudge toward PrivateLink unless they specifically need traffic to appear from their VPC (e.g., for firewall policies). PrivateLink reduces attack surface. If they insist on peering, we need:
- exact subnets to add routes for (list with route table ids)
- any CIDR overlap checks (can't peer overlapping CIDRs)
- clear window for when we'll add routes (we can coordinate a maintenance window)

leah (AE): They also asked about initial test creds — can we provide Hosted API keys for the POC while networking is being finalized?

jules (SE): Yes, provide a short-lived Hosted API key scoped to a sandbox project. Call out: DO NOT send production customer data to hosted key environment until contract & BAA signed. Recommended steps:
- Issue API key with 7-day TTL and throttle limits (e.g., 5 req/s)
- Provide example curl call and sandbox prompts

ami (Cloud Ops): On our side provisioning timeline estimate:
- PrivateLink endpoint service creation + NLB: 1 business day
- Customer creates endpoints + accepts: same day if they provide subnets and account ID
- SG & DNS update: few hours depending on their change window
- End-to-end smoke test: 2-4 hours once endpoints exist

raj (Network Eng): A couple extra operational notes:
- ENI quotas per AZ: ask for DescribeAccountAttributes or just quota numbers. If they hit quota, endpoint creation fails.
- If they use AWS Firewall Manager or central SG policies, the endpoint SG changes might be blocked — ask security ops contact.
- For PrivateLink, we recommend tagging endpoints and subnets with: "redwood:pocteam=acmehealth" for easy cleanup.

leah (AE): Perfect. I'm going to DM AcmeHealth the list. One last ask — any special notes about split-horizon DNS and certs?

jules (SE): Yes:
- If they use private hosted zone for the service DNS, they must ensure their resolver rules point the service hostname to the VPC endpoints.
- Certificate: We serve TLS certs for the endpoint hostname. If they need mutual TLS or client certs, we support mTLS via a separate auth layer — need to enable before test.

ami (Cloud Ops): I'll produce a one-pager with the exact terraform snippet and the service-name to give them. Will attach in the thread in ~2 hours.
